summary: Iteration 3 (Samsung TV control) tested end-to-end. All 10 new backend pytest tests pass; 38/40 total backend tests pass (the 2 failures are pre-existing intermittent HTTP read-timeouts to the preview URL, unrelated to iter-3). Frontend Watch tab TV volume buttons (tv-voldown/tv-mute/tv-volup for all 4 displays), Settings 'Samsung TVs' card with LIVE toggle, per-display field groups (settings-tv-{id}), IP/MAC/HDMI/token inputs, Test connection, and Save all work and persist to config.tv via PUT /api/config. Cleanup: reverted config.tv.live to false and cleared IPs.

minor.issue: Shallow merge at device level: sending {tv:{sets:{tv_living:{...}}}} REPLACES tv.sets rather than merging per-display. Frontend always sends the full sets dict so it works, but a partial API caller could wipe other TVs' config.

action_items: Optional: make PUT /api/config perform a deep-merge (recursive) so partial nested updates to tv.sets don't clobber sibling TVs.
Optional: /api/config/test/tv error string when no IPs are configured currently reads 'No TV IP addresses configured' (matched by test as 'no tv ip'). Consistent with helpful-detail requirement.
critical_code_review_comments: drivers.TVDriver.power(on=True) sends WoL then attempts to also send KEY_HDMI over the SamsungTV WS. If the TV just booted from standby, the WS may not be ready — the try/except in _dispatch catches this and logs 'error', but the UI won't retry. Consider a short delay + retry on power-on.
server.py tv_conn: builds {**per_display_set, 'live': tv.live}. If a driver method later tries conn['sets'] (e.g. by mistake) it won't exist — currently unused, but worth being aware of.
server.py /api/config/test/tv: only tests connectivity to the FIRST TV with an IP (sets[0]). Consider iterating all and returning per-TV status.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_iter3.py (new — 10 tests for Samsung TV: state config, power dual-log, tvkey key/mute/vol, 404 for unknown display, config PUT persistence, test/tv branches for demo/live-unreachable/live-no-ips, regression matrix route)

success_rate.backend: 100% for iter-3 (10/10); 38/40 overall (2 unrelated network timeouts)
